articles.title: The leather jacket comes off: How Jensen Huang lost Nvidia
articles.summary: Thirty-three years. That's how long Nvidia has existed, and how long Jensen Huang ran it.
articles.body: Thirty-three years. That's how long Nvidia has existed, and how long Jensen Huang ran it. For most of those years, you could have sat next to him on a flight and not known who he was. Gamers knew the name on their GeForce cards, and the tech crowd knew the man behind them. Almost nobody knew that his wife, Lori, had given up her own chip design career at Silicon Graphics, where she was paid more than he was, so he could build the company.Then 2022 happened, to all of us and to Huang. Artificial intelligence stopped being a lab experiment and became the thing every government, company and investor wanted a piece of, and nearly all of them needed Nvidia's chips to get it. Huang's early bets had put him right in the middle of it, holding the one thing everybody wanted.Nvidia's chips powered the boom, and Huang made sure Nvidia's money did too. Through an investment portfolio worth about $99 billion, he struck deals with nearly every company that had anything to do with artificial intelligence, from frontier labs to cloud providers, and more than once with companies that then turned around and spent the money on Nvidia chips.Nvidia became the most valuable company on the planet. Its CEO became a celebrity who could no longer walk through a trade show without being mobbed for autographs.The black leather jacket came along for the ride. Huang had been wearing one for at least 20 years, these days picked out by Lori and their daughter, Madison, and judging by his keynotes, it makes up most of his wardrobe. Once he became famous, so did the jacket. In July, one of them sold at Sotheby's for $960,000, 16 times its high estimate, which tells you how the market was valuing anything Huang touched. Jensen Huang was now the man in the leather jacket.By December 2023, he knew Alice Huang, a former Chinese TV reporter who ran one of Nvidia's biggest customers in Southeast Asia.On November 8, he admitted to the affair. On November 12, he was out. The spy story alone didn't do it, because as late as November 9 his board, the president and half of Silicon Valley were still in his corner.Founders this powerful lose their companies only when they lose their boards, and by the night of November 11 Huang had handed Nvidia's directors three reasons to let him go: his affair had become a national security question about Nvidia's China business, he had built a company with no way to sideline him short of removing him, and he had broken a rule they could not look past.Huang's affair ran straight through Nvidia's most sensitive businessPlenty of CEOs have survived an affair. Plenty have not, and Huang now counts among them. Very few, though, have had one with an executive whose company was already under federal investigation for possibly smuggling their products into China.That is what set Alice Huang (no relation, before you ask) apart. Her company, Megaspeed, was set up in Singapore in 2023 and went on to buy more than $4.8 billion worth of Nvidia chips from June 2024, taking delivery of more than 200 shipments in a single year. That is a lot of hardware for a company most of the industry had never heard of. It reportedly rented that computing power to Alibaba, giving China a back door to chips Nvidia cannot sell there directly.By September 2025, the Commerce Department was investigating whether Megaspeed had helped smuggle restricted Nvidia chips into China. Nvidia kept selling to it anyway, which, for a company that prides itself on seeing years ahead, was a remarkably short-sighted call. That investigation is what led US officials to start watching Alice Huang, and to find her in contact with Huang.Their meetings were hardly cloak-and-dagger. In June 2024, after Computex, the two drank whiskey with other artificial intelligence executives at a Taipei bar, and the photo ended up on LinkedIn. A year later, local media photographed her kissing him on the cheek at a dinner in the same city.Alice Huang herself is a different story. Remarkably little is known about her, and her background is largely absent from the Chinese internet. The man she is accused of targeting has fans wearing sweaters with his face on them, while she has managed to leave barely a trace.The New York Times later reported that a memo drafted under Secretary of State Marco Rubio this spring cited intelligence that she had been recruited by China's Ministry of State Security to get close to Huang and nudge Nvidia toward selling its most advanced chips to China. China's embassy has called the reporting "nothing but smears against China," and she has not responded to requests for comment.Set that against Huang's last few years in Washington, where the leather jacket became a familiar sight at the White House and Lori a quiet presence beside him at state dinners.He was the industry's most persistent advocate for selling artificial intelligence chips to China, and in 2025 he talked President Donald Trump into rolling back a ban, then struck a deal that handed the US government a 25 percent cut of sales. He did draw a line at Blackwell and the upcoming Rubin. All the while, he was in a relationship with the woman officials believed was sent to influence that very argument.Trump was briefed in October 2025 and did nothing. Two months later, he approved more powerful Nvidia chip sales to China, and this May he invited Huang on a state visit to Beijing. On November 8, he said he had no regrets. "He dealt with somebody, but you know, so does everybody else," he said. Others were less relaxed. Representative Michael McCaul called it "a classic move from the CCP's playbook," and Senator Elizabeth Warren said Huang and the board "owe Congress answers."Until that week, Huang had denied any affair. He had been brushing off questions about it internally since late 2025, and as recently as October called the relationship "all completely normal and not unusual." It took a report on November 6 that the relationship was romantic, and a visit to his house from Nvidia's general counsel, Tim Teter, for him to finally come clean. For a CEO who has made a point of giving his executives feedback in front of everyone, he had kept this one entirely to himself.His memo on November 8 opened with Lori and their children. "I was unfaithful to my wife," he wrote. "There is no excuse for what I did." A few lines later, he was "committed to protecting Nvidia and supporting America's national security" and "proud and grateful to be an American." Those are not lines a chief executive usually needs to put in an apology for an affair, and none of them could answer the question now hanging over every China decision he had touched.Nobody at Nvidia could tell Huang no, until his own lawyer didWhen a chief executive is caught in a scandal like this, there is usually a halfway step. He takes leave, a deputy runs the company for a few weeks, the board investigates, and everyone buys time.At Nvidia, that step did not exist, and Huang built it that way. He had more than 60 direct reports and a hand in every part of the business, and his son, daughter and son-in-law all worked at the company. His senior executives ran specific products and technologies, not divisions big enough to prepare anyone to run the whole thing.Succession planning came up over the years, former executives have said, and Huang resisted it. In 2023, he said he could run Nvidia for another three or four decades. For a company selling the chips behind artificial intelligence that can supposedly do almost anyone's job, Nvidia had made no plans for anyone to do Huang's.Even after Huang confessed, most of the board did not want to take a public stance, according to people familiar with the matter. It took Teter, who is also the board's secretary, to tell them they had to.So on November 8, the board opened an investigation, declared its "confidence in Jensen and his leadership team," and left him running the company while it investigated him. A spokesperson added that Huang was "committed to continuing to lead Nvidia as CEO without interruption."That arrangement could not last, because it tied the directors' fate to his. Nvidia's 10 board members had served a combined 161 years, many of them beside Huang since the 1990s, and very little of it, by the look of things, spent saying no. A board that close to its CEO, investigating him while he still ran the show, looked less like an inquiry and more like a family meeting.By November 9, a class-action shareholder lawsuit had been filed and the stock was down about a third from its early October peak, more than $1.5 trillion in value gone. With no way to sideline him, the board was left with two options: stand behind Huang completely, or remove him completely. Huang had made sure there was no easier choice.Once there were two affairs, the board stopped waiting for a thirdWhat finally settled it had nothing to do with China.Until then, Huang's defenders had one argument that worked: he was the victim here. Trump kept making that case, calling Huang an "honorable man" who didn't know Alice Huang was a Chinese agent. Even Trump, though, had left himself some room. "I just know he's a fine person," he said, "but you never know what's going on."On November 11, The Times reported, citing five people who worked at Nvidia, that Huang had also had an extramarital relationship with Kimberly Powell, the company's vice president of healthcare, who reported directly to him. In March, months after US officials had started watching his relationship with Alice Huang, Huang and Powell were captured on video being affectionate at a San Jose hotel during GTC, the Nvidia conference where Huang takes the stage in his jacket every year. Powell, who is married, has not responded to requests for comment.Earlier this year, Huang had told an interviewer that Lori had been "to every conference, every speech" of his career. "Every moment of Nvidia, she was there," he said.Judging the Alice Huang affair meant weighing intelligence the board could only see in pieces. The Powell relationship needed no security clearance. Nvidia's code of conduct tells employees to steer clear of conflicts arising from "personal relationships," and many companies bar managers from relationships with people who report to them outright. For the first time, the board had a case it could decide under its own rules.It also had the start of a pattern. One relationship can be written off as a lapse. A second, surfacing within days of the first, is what makes people start looking for more, the way two bees in the kitchen usually mean there is a hive somewhere close.The directors met remotely, late into the night.On November 12, Huang resigned as president, CEO and director, effective immediately. The man in the leather jacket was just Jensen Huang again.Resigned is the polite word. By the end of that meeting, Huang had been given no choice, and the man famous for his grip on every detail of Nvidia was, according to a person familiar with the situation, answering with "whatever" and "I don't care."The announcement of his ouster did not carry a single word from him, an unusual silence from a man whose keynotes routinely run past two hours. Four days earlier, he had promised employees he would "work to earn back your confidence." He never got the chance.Investors were in no mood to mourn: the shares fell another 5.5 percent that day. Within hours of the ouster, the board's caution started to look like foresight. Reuters reported, citing two people familiar with the matter, that Huang had also had an intimate relationship with a second Nvidia employee, whom it did not name. Nvidia declined to comment.Had the board kept him, it would have spent the week before earnings defending a CEO with three relationships to explain and a congressional briefing to attend. Instead, the report landed on a former chief executive.Huang is out of Nvidia, but nowhere near out of the storyCFO Colette Kress will run the company while keeping her current job, and Harvey C. Jones becomes the first board chair in Nvidia's history. It took the company 33 years, and a scandal, to decide it needed one. Jones said he expected Nvidia's operations to "continue without interruption," the same word used four days earlier to promise that Huang was not going anywhere. Kress has called an all-hands meeting for November 18, the day after quarterly results.The search for a permanent CEO is on, and the names doing the rounds, from Kress and Nvidia's Ian Buck to Apple's Johny Srouji, AMD's Lisa Su and Arm's Rene Haas, already make a list as long as the shortlist for the next James Bond. Whoever gets the part inherits the world's most important artificial intelligence company, and possibly a few more headlines about the man who had it before. The leather jacket, mercifully, is not part of the package.Three relationships have been reported in little more than a week, and it would take a brave director to bet that the reporting stops here. Huang is also expected to testify before Congress in the coming weeks, about Alice Huang and what she might have learnt about Nvidia's chips, and a two-hour keynote will not count as an answer.His memo had ended with a request: "My family bears no responsibility for my choices. I do. Please give them privacy." That privacy will be hard to come by. Madison and Spencer still work at Nvidia. In private, according to people who have spoken with him, Huang has taken to calling himself a "piece of sh--." His main concern now, he says, is his wife.Lori has spent four decades out of the spotlight. At an industry awards dinner in 2021, Huang walked onstage with a bottle of red wine and two glasses while she stayed in the background, as she usually did. Today she is president of the family foundation and co-trustee of a trust holding more than half of his 922 million Nvidia shares, with roughly another $5 billion of Nvidia stock in a trust she controls alone.Huang no longer runs Nvidia, and with speculation already swirling about their 41-year marriage, what happens between him and Lori may now shape his stake in the company more than anything his board decides.Your child uses AI every day. articles.body: At least 11 people were killed and three others injured after a vehicle veered off a mountainous road and plunged into a river in Pakistan-occupied Kashmir's Gilgit-Baltistan region, news agency AP reported, citing rescue officials and police.The accident took place on Thursday night after the driver lost control of the vehicle, local police official Mohammad Afzal said.Rescue teams continued search and rescue operations into early Friday. All 11 bodies and the three injured passengers were later taken to a nearby hospital.Regional chief minister Amjad Hussain expressed grief over the incident in a statement and directed authorities to ensure the best possible medical treatment for the injured.Road accidents are common in Pakistan and in the region under its illegal occupation due to poor road conditions, weak enforcement of traffic laws and unsafe driving practices, particularly in mountainous regions.Last week, a bus collided with a truck in eastern Pakistan, killing 11 people and injuring 33 others.You use AI every day. articles.title: 'We'll get you a new mother': Retired railway employee slits wife’s throat, surrenders with daughters
articles.summary: JAMALPUR: “Your mother is dead, we’ll get you a new mother,” a 55-year-old retired railway loco pilot allegedly told his two young daughters after
articles.body: JAMALPUR: “Your mother is dead, we’ll get you a new mother,” a 55-year-old retired railway loco pilot allegedly told his two young daughters after slitting his 28-year-old wife’s throat at their rented home in Bihar’s Munger district late Wednesday night.The accused later took the girls, aged eight and five, to the local police station and surrendered.The victim, identified as Pooja Devi, was found dead inside a locked room at the couple’s residence near Sadar Bazaar in Jamalpur town, under Adarsh Jamalpur police station limits. Police recovered the suspected murder weapon from the spot and sent the body for post-mortem examination.According to preliminary investigations, the accused allegedly locked the two children in a separate room before attacking his wife. After the murder, he locked the room containing her body, covered it with a sheet and took the children to the police station, where he surrendered.Police suspect the murder was triggered by the accused’s suspicion that Pooja was involved in an extramarital relationship. Investigators, however, said all possible angles were being examined.Meanwhile, Pooja’s family alleged that she had faced domestic harassment and dowry-related torture for several years. Her brother, Shubham, said the family was informed by police late Wednesday night about the murder and the accused’s surrender.“We spoke to Pooja just two days ago, but she did not mention any serious problem,” Shubham said. He alleged that the accused and some of his relatives had been harassing and assaulting her for nearly five years. He also claimed that the accused frequently questioned her character because of the age difference between the couple.Pooja, a resident of Ishakchak in Bhagalpur, married the accused in 2015. The couple had been living in a rented house near Sadar Bazaar with their two daughters.Jamalpur SHO Pankaj Kumar said police were investigating the motive and circumstances behind the crime. articles.title: Massive Microsoft 365 outage disrupts email, Teams, Copilot and more services; while some on internet say, 'take your time'; others see 'attack by ...'
articles.summary: Microsoft users across the world faced massive service disruptions starting November 12 after a major outage affected several Microsoft 365 services
articles.body: Microsoft users across the world faced massive service disruptions starting November 12 after a major outage affected several Microsoft 365 services including Microsoft Outlook, Teams, Copilot, SharePoint Online and OneDrive. This service outage left many users struggling to access emails, send messages and connect to workplace applications. This service outage also triggered a wave of reactions and memes on social media. While some of the users joked about enjoying the unexpected break from work and asked Microsoft engineers to take their time in fixing the issue, others questioned what actually led to this kind of disruption, with some suspecting a possible cyberattack. However, Microsoft has not yet attributed the outage to a cyberattack,Massive Microsoft 365 outage: Here’s how users react to the service disruptionMany users reacted with humour. One person wrote in response to the outage, “Take your time. The peace and quiet is nice LOL.” Others joked it was time for a coffee break. Some users also questioned the cause of the disruption, with speculation circulating online about whether it could be linked to a cyberattack.“Good job with all that outsourcing and downsizing,” said a user.“Not upset bout it. Collapse is needed sometimes hahah,” joked another user.“This global Microsoft outage is looking more and more like a cyber attack by the hour,” posted a user on X.Laura Loomer calls Microsoft outage a national security threatUS President Donald Trump’s aide Laura Loomer has also shared her thoughts on the ongoing Microsoft outage. In a post shared on social media platform X, Loomer described the disruption as a "major national security threat" and questioned the US government's reliance on the company's cloud services. Loomer also claimed that the US federal government including the Department of War works on Microsoft Government Azure. She argued that the service disruption highlighted the risks of deepening on Microsoft for important government infrastructure and also called for the cancellation of the company’s government contracts.Read Laura Loomer’s post herePretty crazy that Microsoft has been down all day. Our entire federal government runs on Microsoft Government Azure. Including the Department of War. This is a major national security threat and I’ve been saying for years now that @Microsoft needs to have all of their government contracts canceled. How many chances is Microsoft going to get? With all of those best and brightest H1B workers at Microsoft, I’m shocked they haven’t fixed the outage yet. 😏I was told they are truly the best.Thousands of users reported about the outageThe outage affected Microsoft's email, workplace communication and cloud-based services, with nearly 130,000 users worldwide reporting problems at the peak, according to outage tracker Downdetector.Users reported difficulties accessing Outlook, sending and receiving emails and loading inboxes. Thousands also reported disruptions to Teams, Microsoft's AI assistant Copilot and other Microsoft 365 applications.Microsoft initially said it was investigating reports of users experiencing problems accessing Exchange Online mailboxes through multiple connection methods.The company later identified elevated load across part of its infrastructure as a likely reason for the connectivity errors. It said several servers had become unexpectedly unavailable after failing automated health checks, shifting additional traffic onto the remaining infrastructure.Microsoft said the elevated load was not being caused by an overall increase in traffic, but by the reduced availability of servers.Why did Microsoft 365 services go downMicrosoft's investigation found that several servers had unexpectedly become unavailable, putting additional pressure on the company's remaining infrastructure. The company said the elevated load was not caused by an increase in user traffic but by the loss of server capacity.In updates shared on X, Microsoft said it was working to bring the affected servers back online. It also paused deployments, redistributed network traffic across its global infrastructure and began restarting affected servers to restore capacity.The company further identified an overwhelmed core process on affected servers as a factor behind the loss of capacity. Microsoft said it was also examining whether rolling back some recent configuration updates could help speed up recovery.Here’s what Microsoft said in its latest update"We’ve monitored the status of the changes applied to improve serviceability and confirmed they're not taking as expected. We’re identifying alternate workstreams that can be applied to increase capacity in the face of sustained traffic management imbalances. More info under EX1550543 and MO1550821 in the Microsoft 365 admin center, as well as if the admin center is not available to you."Your child uses AI every day. But do they understand it? YouTube."The pre-show will be hosted by RDCWorld. articles.title: Centre extends ban on Zakir Naik's Islamic Research Foundation for 5 years
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: Centre has extended the ban on the Islamic Research Foundation (IRF), founded by fugitive Islamic preacher Zakir Naik, for another five years,
articles.body: NEW DELHI: Centre has extended the ban on the Islamic Research Foundation (IRF), founded by fugitive Islamic preacher Zakir Naik, for another five years, declaring the organisation an unlawful association under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA).In a notification issued on Friday, the Union home ministry said the organisation and its members, particularly its founder and president, Dr Zakir Abdul Karim Naik, were allegedly encouraging and assisting followers in promoting enmity, hatred and ill-will between different religious communities. The government said such activities posed a threat to the country's integrity and security.The notification described speeches and statements made by Naik as "inflammatory and subversive", alleging that he was promoting religious hatred and inciting young people belonging to a particular religion in India and abroad to commit terrorist acts.It also said Naik had delivered fundamentalist speeches and made statements before millions of people worldwide through international satellite television networks, the internet, print and social media.The home ministry said that if IRF's activities were not immediately prohibited and controlled, the organisation could continue its subversive activities and reorganise its cadres who had already been convicted. It also warned that the organisation could create communal disharmony, disrupt the country's secular fabric, propagate anti-national sentiments, support terrorism and encourage separatism.IRF was first declared an unlawful association in November 2016 for five years. The ban was subsequently extended in November 2021 for another five-year period. The latest notification comes ahead of the expiry of the existing declaration on November 14, 2026.Naik, who left India in 2016 and is currently based in Malaysia, has faced allegations of promoting religious extremism through his speeches. The IRF has also been under scrutiny over its alleged links to radical activities.Get the latest India News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Sandyford home DIY SOS-style rebuild plan after summer barbecue blaze
articles.summary: A couple in their 80s hope to see their home rebuilt after the massive fire in Sandyford in August.
articles.body:
"We're going to have to get out of here, pronto," was what John Draycott said to wife Veronica as a fire raced towards their home.

The couple escaped with seconds to spare as flames spread through their Sandyford house, which was gutted and later demolished after a barbecue blaze got out of control.

Now, a community-led campaign is aiming to rebuild the house, the worst affected in the fire that tore through the area of Stoke-on-Trent on 13 August amid tinder dry conditions, from the ground up.

Curtis Peters, of TS Domestics, and Javaid Iqbal, from Impact Stoke, hope tradespeople, firms and residents will donate skills, labour and materials for the project, which needs planning permission.

The property, for which the Draycotts were not insured, later had to be pulled down because the fire had left it structurally unstable.

It has left the couple facing the prospect of losing their home entirely, prompting the community-led effort to rebuild it.

Once planning permissions is secured, organisers estimate the rebuild will take about 18 months to complete.

For John, the memories of the fire remain vivid.

"I was in total shock and devastated," he said.

After spotting smoke nearby, he initially believed a building several doors away had caught fire.

"I ran upstairs, looked through the bathroom window, saw three doors away on fire and then started panicking," he told the BBC.

"Within just those few minutes, it spread from three doors away to our corner."

As the fire moved through the garden, Draycott realised they had no time to save any belongings.

"As soon as I saw it coming up through the garden, I turned round to the wife saying: 'Look, we're going to have to get out of here - we've got no choice. We've got time to grab nothing.'"

"We just dashed out the front door," he said.

"I shut the door behind me with the intention of hopefully slowing down the fire, but it didn't make any difference."

"It just whistled through this lot in no time at all. Twenty minutes to half an hour this house was burnt right through completely."

Even Draycott's false teeth were among possessions he lost.

Following the fire, members of the community and staff at The Terrace Dental Clinic helped provide him with a replacement set.

It was that support, organisers say, which showed how much local people wanted to help.

Iqbal said seeing the couple's situation inspired him to act.

"I've seen the couple in their 80s and they were left absolutely hopeless," he said.

"They didn't have insurance and I thought that with me having a construction background and having TS Domestics involved, we could put this together as a community."

Peters said the project would be the largest community initiative he had ever worked on.

"We saw it happen, so we came together and decided let's get it rebuilt," he said.

Organisers said even the foundations were affected by the fire, meaning the house will need to be completely rebuilt.

Peters said the response from the community had already been encouraging, but more help was still needed.

"At first I thought it was a massive project, and it is a massive project, but as soon as we sat down and talked it through, I think it's completely achievable," he said.

"It's going to be so good for the community to see a brand-new house here again."

articles.title: A West Wales couple started an indoor farming business with less than £2,000; within three months, it was profitable and growing over 30 varieties of microgreens and herbs
articles.summary: A West Wales couple turned a small investment into a profitable indoor farming business after spending less than £2,000 on shelves, seeds and trays.
articles.body: A West Wales couple turned a small investment into a profitable indoor farming business after spending less than £2,000 on shelves, seeds and trays. Toni and Alex Borella own and operate Green Up Farm, a hydroponic indoor vertical farm in Ceredigion. They started the business in 2021 after researching the market for microgreens and deciding to grow their own crops.In a 2024 interview with Swansea University, Toni Borella revealed that Green Up Farm grew more than 30 types of microgreens and micro herbs, supplying restaurants and other establishments across West Wales. Reportedly, Green Up Farm became profitable within just three months of its launch.How did a couple start a profitable micro-herb farm with less than £2,000Toni and Alex Borella started Green Up Farm in 2021 after researching the microgreens market. The couple had wanted to start a business and were interested in growing their own crops. They found that microgreens were a large business in the United States before deciding to take the plunge.Their initial spending was less than £2,000, used to buy shelves, seeds and trays. The farm is based in Ceredigion and uses hydroponic indoor vertical farming. Its first client was Crwst, a company in Cardigan where Alex worked at the time. Toni approached the chefs at Crwst with samples of their produce and asked which micro herbs they would like the farm to grow.How did live microgreens become Green Up Farm’s unique selling pointThe most important feedback from chefs was that they wanted live produce. Toni said this became Green Up Farm’s unique selling point because most other growers did not sell live products.She explained that produce which was not sold live had a limited shelf life and could lose quality. The feedback led the couple to adapt their process and focus solely on selling live products.As of 2024, Green Up Farm supplied directly to most mid to high end establishments in West Wales. Its customers included The Nags Head in Abercych, Yr Hens Printworks and Boys and Girls in Cardigan. Toni said communication and consistency were key to the business, particularly when supplies changed.Green Up Farm grew more than 30 types of microgreens and herbsGreen Up Farm sold more than 30 types of microgreens and micro herbs at the time. Its most popular varieties are pea shoots, nasturtium and coriander. The couple continues to look for different flavours, while considering whether a product adds something to a dish before taking it to market. Toni said conversations with chefs often spark trends, with one restaurant’s request sometimes leading others to ask for the same microgreen.Social media also influenced what customers want. One week they might ask for coriander and the next for fennel, making it important for the farm to keep up. The business also offered harvest boxes to local customers with small kitchens.Green Up Farm reduced plastic waste through reusable packagingThe couple moved to Pembrokeshire in 2019 after spending more than 20 years in London. Toni said they wanted to be closer to the coastline and had happy memories of the area from her childhood. Green Up Farm’s sustainability approach included avoiding plastic waste. The farm generated only cardboard waste, while its organic waste was sent to a community garden instead of being thrown into a food bin.Customers return packaging after use, which the couple hygienically clean and reuse. Toni said many customers chose the business because of its approach.How the ARCS partnership helped Green Up Farm explore sustainable packagingGreen Up Farm’s connection with Swansea University’s ARCS team centred on learning how to make its business more sustainable. Co-owner Toni Borella said the farm wanted a better understanding of the circular economy, particularly the use of plastics. The collaboration was expected to provide fact-checking and guidance as the business considered its choices, including plans to introduce a tray made from recycled PET (r-PET). Borella also wanted help communicating circular-economy ideas clearly to customers and social media followers. The farm already reused its packaging by collecting it from customers, cleaning it and using it again. Through the partnership, Green Up Farm hoped to assess whether new materials would genuinely improve its environmental impact while supporting sound business decisions in future.You use AI every day. articles.title: Florida homeowner started with hay bales and a pumpkin; seven years later, his free Halloween attraction spans nearly 5,000 square feet, with handmade tombstones, towering skeletons and hidden speakers
articles.summary: A modest seasonal display has grown into one of the more elaborate Halloween attractions in an Orange Park neighbourhood, bringing together homemade
articles.body: A modest seasonal display has grown into one of the more elaborate Halloween attractions in an Orange Park neighbourhood, bringing together homemade decorations, theatrical effects and a touch of American history. According to News4JAX and the Fleming Island-Orange Park Times, the attraction, known as Bearadise, is the creation of local homeowner Matt McCary, who has spent seven years turning his Halloween hobby into a free experience for families. What began in 2019 with a few hay bales and a pumpkin has evolved into an immersive outdoor display covering nearly 5,000 square feet. The attraction now features a graveyard, handmade tombstones, towering skeletons, overhead cobwebs and hundreds of feet of lighting. Hidden speakers, sound effects and fog machines add to the atmosphere, giving visitors the feeling of walking through a carefully staged Halloween scene.The experience is designed as a walk-through rather than a display to be viewed from the pavement. Visitors follow a paved pathway through the decorated area, entering through a homemade archway before making their way past the various spooky installations. The scale of the project also means that McCary cannot put everything together alone. Around 14 people help unload the decorations, while the electrical arrangements, lighting and other finishing touches take several weeks to complete.The attraction's handmade details are another part of its appeal. McCary has created many of the tombstones himself, even inviting neighbours to contribute to the fun through a contest for humorous grave markers. The display has also developed into a shared community project, with residents helping bring the seasonal installation to life.According to a 2023 community newsletter published by Orange Park Country Club, the attraction was previously known as the Haunted Pathway. Even then, it covered more than 4,000 square feet and featured themed sections including the Boneyard, Spider Alley and Witch Way. The annual event has continued to expand, with new additions introduced over the years.A Halloween attraction with a historical connectionBeyond the skeletons and spooky decorations, Bearadise also has an educational element inspired by McCary's personal connection to Salem, Massachusetts. He married there in October 2013, and the town's association with the infamous Salem witch trials became part of the attraction's theme. One section features QR codes that visitors can scan to access information about the 1692 witch trials, including details about individuals who were accused, tried and executed. The addition gives families an opportunity to learn about a significant chapter in American history while exploring the Halloween-themed setting.Although the attraction is primarily designed for evening visits, its lighting is sometimes switched on earlier to make it more accessible to younger children who might find the darker, more theatrical effects frightening.Today, Bearadise reportedly welcomes around 250 trick-or-treaters annually. Its popularity is also evident beyond Halloween, with local children recognising the property as the neighbourhood's Halloween house even during the summer months.For McCary, the attraction is ultimately about creating a place where families can share the excitement of the season. What began as a small decorating project has become a neighbourhood tradition, bringing together residents through creativity, nostalgia and a shared love of Halloween.You use AI every day. articles.title: Nvidia employees want Jensen Huang back as CEO; internal suggestion box post draws over 1,600 comments: We are all humans and can make mistakes, Jensen did so many good things and he...
articles.summary: Jensen Huang may have stepped down as Nvidia CEO, but a large part of the company's workforce isn't ready to move on.
articles.body: Jensen Huang may have stepped down as Nvidia CEO, but a large part of the company's workforce isn't ready to move on. An internal suggestion box post urging Nvidia's board to weigh employee sentiment before deciding Huang's future has drawn more than 1,600 comments, with most of them backing his return to the top job, according to internal correspondence reviewed by Wired.The post was written by a longtime Nvidia engineer before Huang resigned. It has since become a rallying point for staff who want the 63-year-old cofounder reinstated, despite the multiple reported extramarital affairs that led to his abrupt exit. "If you believe in the mission, bring back THE boss," wrote one anonymous commenter. Another added, "We are all humans and can make mistakes. Jensen did so many good things and he needs a second chance."Nvidia employee's companywide email backs Jensen HuangThe support hasn't stayed inside the suggestion box. One employee sent an email to the entire company demanding transparency into Huang's exit. "I stand by Jensen," the staffer wrote. "Not because I believe any person is infallible, but because I refuse to believe that standing for fairness must mean standing at a distance from someone whose leadership has meant so much to us."The same email went a step further: "If America fails the man who helped build its future, then this world does not deserve Jensen Huang."The employee behind the email couldn't be reached for comment, while the engineer who wrote the suggestion box post declined to comment. Nvidia and its new board chair, Harvey Jones, did not immediately respond to Wired's requests for comment.Why Jensen Huang resigned as Nvidia CEOHuang, who had led Nvidia since its founding in 1993, wrote to employees on Sunday admitting he had been "unfaithful to [his] wife" and that there was "no excuse." The email followed reports of an affair with a suspected Chinese intelligence asset.The board announced his resignation on Thursday morning, after reports of an alleged second affair, this time with a direct report. That employee has not commented on the matter. Reuters has since reported an alleged affair with yet another Nvidia employee. Huang hasn't said anything about these reports since his Sunday email.The fallout has been heavy. Nvidia has lost about $1 trillion in market value since the allegations surfaced. US lawmakers and the FBI have opened investigations, and the episode has raised the prospect of fresh export controls on chips. The board, made up largely of early Nvidia investors and Huang's longtime confidants, has named chief financial officer Colette Kress as interim CEO. Former Synopsys CEO Harvey Jones is the new chair.Nvidia staff say the company needs its founderWork inside Nvidia has carried on as usual this week, but the resignation left many employees stunned. Within hours, about two dozen staffers posted on LinkedIn in support of Huang, with one calling their faith in his leadership unwavering. Over the same period, Wired couldn't find a single post from an Nvidia employee supporting his exit.One employee, who has been at the company for a couple of years and wasn't authorised to speak publicly, told Wired the push for Huang's reinstatement is widespread. They worry Nvidia will suffer in the long run without its founder in charge and say the board must bring him back. "Nvidia is Nvidia because of Jensen," the employee said.Much of the frustration comes down to timing. Many employees expected the board's investigation to wrap up before any big changes were made. The suggestion box post had asked the board to share its findings with staff and formally gather their views "about Jensen's continuing as our CEO."That never happened. Huang stepped down just as the inquiry had begun, and staff are still looking for answers on why he left before it was done.Your child uses AI every day. But do they understand it? articles.title: A 4,000-year-old wall, an ancient bank and a ditch emerged from Morocco’s Oued Beht ridge, clarifying a puzzle first recorded in 1936
articles.summary: Discoveries at Morocco's Oued Beht reveal a 4,000-year-old wall, a defensive structure reshaping our understanding of ancient North African societies and their connections with Europe.
articles.body: Researchers uncovered a previously unknown chapter of history after discovering a large-scale construction at Oued Beht in 2023. It lies in North Africa beyond the Nile Valley, and researchers estimated it to be about 4,000 to 3,500 years old. According to the research paper titled “Expanding Oued Beht: Final Neolithic, Bronze Age, medieval and later discoveries from excavation and survey in 2023”, the construction was likely used as a defensive structure. But against what or whom is not yet determined. Prior to this discovery, researchers at the Oued Beht Archaeological Project had already established two things. Firstly, the agricultural complex was likely the largest and earliest in Africa outside the Nile Valley, as per a 2024 report in The Conversation by archaeologists Cyprian Broodbank, Giulio Lucarini and Youssef Bokbot. Secondly, its inception was dated to between 3400 BCE and 2900 BCE, per the same report. The paper says six new trenches were opened in 2023, including a 5 × 5 m exposure beside earlier French-Moroccan excavations, and that Trench 3/3.1 was crucial for untangling “Wall B1.” In that trench, the team identified prehistoric foundations for a daub-and-possibly-stone wall, a later stone-built wall above it, a multi-phased embankment and a parallel ditch, with radiocarbon dates and prehistoric pottery used to refine the sequence.Who were they keeping out? In 1936, French archaeologist Armand Ruhlmann recorded three walls crossing the Oued Beht ridge in northwest Morocco, as reported in the research paper. He interpreted them as a defensive barrier, but their age remained uncertain. In 2023, after new excavations at the site, researchers deepened their knowledge of the region. The findings come from the Oued Beht Archaeological Project’s third field season. The team examined Wall B1, the largest of four built alignments in the ridge’s southern section, which differs from the three walls Ruhlmann recorded. What appeared to be one substantial wall proved to be several features, including wall foundations, an earthen embankment and a ditch. Studying the sites gave researchers the vantage point of looking at the everyday rural life of prehistoric and medieval times, often overlooked by history books.Researchers opined the wall may have been built to safeguard land and resources from rival neighbours rather than foreign invaders, though the exact threat remained elusive. The wall may also have served to exert control and power. Local communities wanted to stake their claim on important locations and leverage the mobility of those who passed through the area. The wall suggested that organised defence in the Maghreb was much older and more complex than researchers previously thought. As per the study, people had returned to the exact ridge at Oued Beht between the 11th and 13th centuries CE and rebuilt the wall. Along with it, they had also established a small village on the top of a hill and sandwiched a cemetery right between the village and the wall.A bustling gathering point of Northwest AfricaUp to this point, little was known about the ancient history of the Maghreb, which now comprises Morocco, Algeria and Tunisia. Between 3400 and 2900 BCE, Oued Beht was a hub of farming and craft-making. The people who used the site farmed barley and wheat, raised livestock, and were major producers of stone axes and painted pots. However, researchers were unsure if these people actually lived there or were just visitors. This suggests northwest Morocco may have been a regional meeting point.Clues beneath the surface and across the seaIn the 1930s, archaeologists had noticed old linear walls and embankments at Oued Beht, but they did not know their age until the recent excavation, as per the paper. After radiocarbon dating of the deposits, researchers posited the timelines for the ditches, embankments and walls. As per the results, they were built during the Bronze Age. This may make them among the oldest defensive structures in North Africa outside of Egypt.Moreover, the communities in the region did not live in isolation, as believed. Across the water, between 2200 and 1550 BCE, people in Southern Spain and Portugal, known as Argaric societies, were pioneering complex infrastructure and planned towns on hilltops. The hallmark of their work was characterised by advanced metallurgy, particularly bronze production. Because communities in northwest Africa (Oued Beht) lived in the same parallel timeline as their European counterparts, researchers compared their fortified hilltop settlements. This may help explain the defensive wall system built on a strategic ridge at Oued Beht. Following another trail of clues in the deep storage pits helped researchers establish another link between North Africa and Europe. The same types of pits used for storing food or goods were found in Iberia during that period, The Conversation reported.You use AI every day. Now get your AI Quotient. Take the AIQ test.

articles.title: Jensen Huang's resignation, Chinese cyberattack and rogue AI: The conspiracy theories surrounding Microsoft outage
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: A global Microsoft outage that disrupted Outlook, Teams, Copilot and several other services has triggered a wave of conspiracy theories online,
articles.body: NEW DELHI: A global Microsoft outage that disrupted Outlook, Teams, Copilot and several other services has triggered a wave of conspiracy theories online, with social media users linking the disruption to Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang's departure, alleging a possible Chinese cyberattack and even speculating about a rogue AI agent.The outage, which began late Thursday (November 12) and continued into Friday, affected Microsoft's email, workplace communication and cloud-based services, leaving users across several countries struggling to access essential applications. While Microsoft attributed the disruption to infrastructure and server capacity problems, speculation about a possible cyberattack and other causes gained traction on social media.One theory linked the outage to Huang's departure from Nvidia, suggesting that the timing of the two developments was more than a coincidence. Another claimed that China could be behind an attack on US communications infrastructure, while some users questioned whether an artificial intelligence agent had gone rogue.However, Microsoft has said there is no indication that the disruption was caused by malicious activity or a cyberattack.Jensen Huang's exit and Microsoft outage: Why are users connecting the two?The timing of the Microsoft disruption and the developments surrounding Huang's departure from Nvidia became a talking point on X.A user named Reese posted: "Jensen Huang stepped down and immediately after there is a global Microsoft outage. #noticing"The post suggested a connection between the two developments but offered no evidence to support the claim.The speculation comes amid a controversy surrounding Huang's departure from Nvidia, which has also drawn attention to the company's business relationships, national security concerns and the US technology sector.However, there is no evidence linking Huang's departure to Microsoft's technical problems.China attack theory: Is Beijing behind the outage?Another conspiracy theory circulating online suggested that the outage could be part of a Chinese cyber operation targeting US communications infrastructure.US political commentator Valentina Gomez claimed that the simultaneous developments involving Huang and Microsoft were not a coincidence.In a post on X, she wrote:"🚨Jensen Huang & Microsoft going DOWN on the same day is not a coincidence-911 systems are currently down-Credit cards/banking will go offline-If nuclear plants go offline for too long, it WILL be a huge problem.I think this is China attacking US communications grid"The post also raised concerns about the possible impact of a prolonged outage on emergency services, banking and critical infrastructure.However, no evidence has emerged to support the claim that China was responsible for the disruption. Microsoft has explicitly said its investigation has found no indication of malicious or cyber activity.Rogue AI theory: Did an AI agent cause the disruption?Another theory circulating online suggested that an artificial intelligence system or autonomous AI agent could have triggered the disruption.The speculation gained attention as Microsoft's Copilot and other AI-related services were among the affected products.However, the company has not reported any evidence of an AI agent causing the outage. Microsoft has instead pointed to server availability, infrastructure load and an overwhelmed core process as the reasons behind the disruption.Charles Lamanna, executive vice-president of Copilot, Agents and Platform at Microsoft, addressed the speculation in a post on X."We regret that today’s outages caused disruptions for our customers, and we are working to address the issue. We will continue to share more information as soon as we have it, and for now I can confirm that there is no indication this is the result of malicious or cyber activity".What is Microsoft saying about the outage?Microsoft initially said it was investigating reports of users facing difficulties accessing Exchange Online mailboxes through multiple connection methods.Its subsequent investigation found that several servers had unexpectedly become unavailable after failing automated health checks. This reduced the available server capacity and pushed additional traffic onto the remaining infrastructure, resulting in connectivity problems.The company clarified that the elevated load was not caused by an overall increase in user traffic but by the reduced availability of servers.Microsoft also identified an overwhelmed core process on affected servers as a factor behind the capacity loss.The company said it was attempting to restore services by bringing affected servers back online, redistributing network traffic and exploring alternative recovery measures.However, its initial attempts to restore normal operations did not deliver the expected results.In an update on Friday, Microsoft 365 Status said: "We’ve monitored the status of the changes applied to improve serviceability and confirmed they're not taking as expected. We’re identifying alternate workstreams that can be applied to increase capacity in the face of sustained traffic management imbalances. More info under EX1550543 and MO1550821 in the Microsoft 365 admin center, as well as if the admin center is not available to you."Microsoft said it was continuing to work on restoring the affected services.Laura Loomer questions Microsoft's government contractsThe outage also triggered criticism of Microsoft's role in providing technology infrastructure to US government agencies.Political commentator Laura Loomer questioned the dependence of federal departments on Microsoft's cloud services and called for a review of the company's government contracts.In a post on X, she wrote: "Pretty crazy that Microsoft has been down all day. Our entire federal government runs on Microsoft Government Azure. Including the Department of War. This is a major national security threat and I’ve been saying for years now that @Microsoft needs to have all of their government contracts canceled. How many chances is Microsoft going to get? With all of those best and brightest H1B workers at Microsoft, I’m shocked they haven’t fixed the outage yet. 😏 I was told they are truly the best."Her remarks added to the debate over the risks of government agencies relying heavily on a single technology provider.How widespread was the Microsoft outage?The disruption affected several Microsoft 365 services, including Outlook, Teams, Copilot, SharePoint Online and OneDrive.According to Downdetector, nearly 130,000 users worldwide reported problems at the peak of the outage.Users reported difficulties accessing email accounts, sending and receiving messages, loading inboxes and joining workplace meetings.The disruption also affected government departments and other organisations in different countries.Australia's Department of Foreign Affairs and Trade issued a notice directing urgent sanctions-related enquiries to the Australian Sanctions Office by telephone.The Department of Agriculture, Fisheries and Forestry also warned that clients might be unable to send or receive emails through its systems.While the outage prompted concerns about the vulnerability of digital infrastructure and the dependence of organisations on cloud-based services, the conspiracy theories circulating online remain unsubstantiated.Microsoft's investigation, so far, points to technical and infrastructure-related problems rather than a confirmed cyberattack.You use AI every day. articles.title: TOI Bharat Makers Awards 2027: Times of India launches national platform to celebrate 35 categories of India’s builders, innovators and changemakers
articles.summary: India's growth story is shaped by more than its biggest companies, well-known entrepreneurs and influential leaders.
articles.body: India's growth story is shaped by more than its biggest companies, well-known entrepreneurs and influential leaders. Across the country, individuals, small businesses, educators, healthcare professionals, artisans, social workers and innovators are contributing to change in their own ways. Recognising these efforts and bringing their stories to a national audience, The Times of India is launching the TOI Bharat Makers Awards, a national recognition platform celebrating people and organisations helping build a progressive India.The initiative aims to bring together achievers from diverse backgrounds and sectors, giving recognition to contributions that often go beyond conventional measures of success. With 35 award categories, the platform will spotlight individuals, entrepreneurs, businesses, institutions and grassroots changemakers whose work is creating an impact across the country.From a business founder building an enterprise to a teacher transforming a classroom or an artisan preserving traditional crafts, the awards seek to recognise people whose efforts are contributing to India's development.A national platform for India's diverse achieversThe TOI Bharat Makers Awards has been conceptualised to celebrate the people who are driving progress across different parts of the country. The platform recognises that nation-building is not limited to a particular profession, industry or geographical location. Its 35 categories cover a wide range of fields, including entrepreneurship, business, education, healthcare, innovation, public service, social impact, arts, culture, sports, agriculture and institutional initiatives.The awards also include flagship honours such as Bharat Maker of the Year, Lifetime Achievement in Nation-Building and the People's Choice Award. Other categories recognise entrepreneurs, women achievers, young innovators, farmers, social workers, educational institutions, NGOs and organisations working towards community development.The initiative is open to individuals, groups and organisations whose work is based in India, irrespective of their scale or location. This means a small-town entrepreneur, a grassroots organisation, an independent innovator or an established institution can all find a place on the platform, provided their work meets the relevant category's eligibility criteria.Recognising impact, originality and long-term contributionAn important aspect of the awards is the emphasis on merit-based recognition. Entries will be evaluated by an independent jury against a published scoring framework, ensuring that achievements are assessed on the basis of their contribution and measurable impact. The evaluation will consider five parameters: impact, originality, scale and reach, sustainability, and integrity. Impact carries 30 marks, originality 25, scale and reach 20, sustainability 15, and integrity 10.The jury will assess how effectively an individual or organisation has addressed a challenge, the uniqueness of its approach, the extent of its contribution and the potential for its work to create lasting change. The jury panel brings together professionals and leaders from enterprise, public life, healthcare, education, social impact, media and the arts. Among the listed members are AI innovation leader Shantanu Gaur, actor and host Tanuj Virwani, healthcare entrepreneur Dr Shuchin Bajaj, Gauranga Das, journalist and author Dr Tabeenah Anjum, entrepreneur Rashi Narang, Kanchan Gupta, civil servant Shraddha Joshi Sharma and social impact leader Asmita Satyarthi.How the nomination and selection process will workThe awards follow a structured nomination and evaluation process. Interested individuals can nominate themselves or put forward someone whose work they believe deserves recognition. Organisations can also submit entries in relevant categories. Nominations opened in October 2026 and will remain open until December 31, 2026. Applicants need to select the appropriate category, provide a brief description of their work and submit supporting evidence. This may include achievements, photographs, figures, media coverage or references that establish the impact of their contribution.Once submitted, entries will undergo an initial screening to check eligibility and completeness before moving to the jury evaluation stage. The platform will also feature a People's Choice Award, which will be decided through public voting on TOI Bharat among the published nominees. Voting is scheduled between January 1 and January 12, 2027.The nomination process includes different participation tiers for individuals and institutions. The entry fee starts at Rs 30,000 for the Nominee category, while Featured Nominee entries cost Rs 50,000 for up to two categories. Institutional entries are priced at Rs 1 lakh for up to two institutional categories, with applicable GST. Importantly, paying the nomination fee does not guarantee an award. All entries receive equal consideration from the jury, irrespective of the nomination tier selected. The winners will be determined through the independent evaluation process.Winners to be honoured in New Delhi during Republic Day weekThe culmination of the TOI Bharat Makers Awards will take place at the Summit and Awards Night scheduled for January 22, 2027, in New Delhi, ahead of the 78th Republic Day celebrations. articles.title: Microsoft 365 outage status update: Company reports 'positive results' in fix for Outlook, Teams and other 365 services
articles.summary: Microsoft says its fix for the global Microsoft 365 outage is finally starting to work.
articles.body: Microsoft says its fix for the global Microsoft 365 outage is finally starting to work. More than 12 hours after users around the world lost access to Outlook, Teams and other Microsoft 365 services, the company said on Friday that it is seeing "positive results" for server stability. A full recovery, however, is still some way off.In its latest update on the Microsoft 365 service health page, the company said it has applied an "upstream authentication/routing configuration component patch" to a portion of its infrastructure. Put simply, the fix targets how users connect to Microsoft's servers. Microsoft said it will keep monitoring the patch and is working to roll it out to servers supporting active regions as they come back online. There is still no timeline for when services will be fully restored.Outlook and Teams stayed down because Microsoft's servers kept failing health checksThe update comes shortly after Microsoft admitted it had seen only "marginal success" and was adding virtual machines to expand capacity.The trouble began around 11:30 pm IST on Thursday, when users in the Americas started reporting that they could not reach their Exchange Online mailboxes. Microsoft soon confirmed that users in any region could be affected. Impacted services include Exchange Online, Microsoft Teams, SharePoint Online, Microsoft 365 Copilot and Microsoft Defender XDR. On the consumer side, Outlook.com, OneDrive, OneNote, Microsoft To Do and Microsoft 365 for the web have also seen problems.Microsoft's early updates pointed to elevated load on its infrastructure. It later clarified that traffic had not spiked. Instead, a number of servers had gone offline unexpectedly, putting pressure on the ones still running. The servers were failing automated health checks, and some that engineers brought back went unresponsive again as soon as traffic hit them. At one point, the company conceded its fix was "not taking as expected". It paused all deployments, moved traffic to other routes and blocked certain types of traffic in some regions to ease the load.Microsoft says the outage is not a cyberattackMicrosoft has repeatedly said there is no sign of a hack behind the disruption. "As of now, we are not aware of any malicious activity that is causing this incident," the company said in its status update. Microsoft executive Charles Lamanna also said on social media that there was "no indication this is the result of malicious or cyber activity".The company has promised a Post-Incident Report once the issue is resolved. It will detail the root cause and the repairs Microsoft plans to make so the same failure does not repeat.Microsoft 365 outage disrupts airlines, AI companies and governments worldwideThe fallout has gone well beyond office inboxes. In India, IndiGo and Akasa Air said their email support services were affected. AI companies OpenAI and Anthropic reported issues with Microsoft connectors.In Japan, government email services went down, and digital minister Toshiharu Furukawa said officials would use text messages as a stopgap. Economy minister Ryosei Akazawa said the disruption had a "major impact" on the country.Australia's spy agency and federal police were among the organisations hit there, and a risk advisory firm estimated the cost to Australian businesses at billions of dollars. In the UK, several police forces asked people to call 101 instead of filing crime reports online, while schools told parents to phone in absences. Traders in Singapore and fund managers in Taiwan also fell back on phone calls and WhatsApp to confirm deals.For now, users may still have trouble connecting to Microsoft 365 apps, and recovery is likely to be gradual as clients reconnect. IT admins can follow updates under MO1550821 in the Microsoft 365 admin center, or on status.cloud.microsoft if the admin center is unavailable.The bigger question is whether the patched servers hold up once they take on full traffic. That is exactly where Microsoft's earlier attempts fell apart overnight.Your child uses AI every day. But do they understand it? Find out in the TOI AI Masterclass.

articles.title: An Indiana worker died in a 2025 crash, leaving a widow, five children and a wrongful-death claim; after a battle over who would control his estate, a November 12 appeals court backed his daughter as sole administrator
articles.summary: An Indiana appeals court has upheld the removal of Rebecca Johnson as co-personal representative of Shane Fields' estate, leaving his daughter Hailey
articles.body: An Indiana appeals court has upheld the removal of Rebecca Johnson as co-personal representative of Shane Fields' estate, leaving his daughter Hailey Daniels in charge. In its November 12 ruling, the court found that Johnson's refusal to follow court directions and cooperate with Daniels had affected the administration of the estate.According to the details of the case given in the judgement, Fields died in a road accident in Kentucky on January 31, 2025, while working for R&S Excavating. He was survived by his wife, Breanna, whom he married in 2023, and five children. His three adult daughters were Hailey Daniels, Paige Fields and Ryann Fields. His sons were Landon Patterson and Elijah Barnhart.The estate had few assets. Its main potential value came from a wrongful-death claim linked to the accident. The person appointed to represent the estate would therefore play an important role in pursuing the claim.Johnson, a family friend nominated by Breanna, sought appointment as personal representative in February 2025. Daniels opposed her request and filed a petition to take charge of the estate. In July, the trial court appointed both women as co-personal representatives. Their disagreement soon extended to the choice of lawyers for the wrongful-death case.Dispute over legal representationMorgan and Morgan (M&M) filed a wrongful-death complaint in Kentucky on July 23, 2025, naming Johnson as the estate's representative and sole plaintiff. An amended complaint filed on August 5 added Breanna as an individual plaintiff.Daniels wanted the estate to hire local lawyer Robert Miles and his firm, Kolb Roellgen & Traylor LLP (KR&T). Johnson questioned Miles' experience and raised concerns about the firm's fees.KR&T proposed a fixed contingency fee of 33%. M&M initially proposed 30%, but its fee could increase at later stages of the case, including an appeal.The trial court asked the two representatives to agree on a law firm. When they failed to reach an agreement, it selected KR&T. Johnson challenged the decision and sought permission to appeal it, but the trial court rejected her requests.The court also raised concerns about Johnson making decisions without consulting Daniels. It directed her to explain why she should not face contempt proceedings or removal, noting that she appeared to have consulted Breanna instead of her co-representative.Concerns over estate records and payrollThe disagreement also involved the handling of estate records. In September 2025, Johnson filed an inventory without discussing it with Daniels. Daniels told the court that it left out items including a gun safe, guns and an iPhone.Johnson had also obtained an employer identification number for the estate without consulting Daniels. She shared it only after the court issued an order seeking an explanation of her conduct.Another concern involved Fields' wages at R&S Excavating. The court proceedings showed that his wages had been issued in Breanna's name. It was alleged that this arrangement allowed Fields to continue receiving workers' compensation benefits from a previous employer while working at R&S.Johnson said she learnt about the arrangement after Fields' death, when a tax document showed income in Breanna's name. Daniels filed a police report. Johnson said she contacted R&S's workers' compensation insurer to ask about death benefits.The court also considered a possible conflict involving Johnson's husband, who worked at R&S and had been Fields' supervisor. Johnson acknowledged that legal action against the company could affect her husband's employment.Daniels sought Johnson's removal on December 9, 2025, citing the handling of estate records, the dispute over lawyers and her failure to follow court directions.At a January hearing, the trial court told Johnson that she had to sign KR&T's fee agreement or face removal. Johnson remained unwilling to sign unless Miles worked with more experienced lawyers.On March 4, the trial court removed Johnson and appointed Daniels as the sole personal representative. It approved KR&T's fee agreement, cancelled any agreement Johnson had entered into without Daniels' approval and directed Johnson to provide a final account and hand over the estate records.Appeals court rejects Johnson's challengeJohnson argued before the Indiana Court of Appeals that Breanna's nomination gave her priority under state law to represent the estate.The appeals court acknowledged that the surviving spouse's nominee had priority under the relevant law. However, it said this did not prevent a trial court from removing a personal representative found unsuitable.The judges found that Johnson had repeatedly refused to follow the trial court's directions on legal representation. They said she was required to comply with the orders unless they were overturned on appeal.The court also noted that the dispute had delayed the wrongful-death and workers' compensation claims. It said Johnson's conduct went beyond a disagreement between co-representatives and interfered with the administration of the estate.The concerns over the payroll arrangement, her husband's employment, the estate inventory and her dealings with M&M also supported the trial court's decision, the appeals court said.Johnson had further argued that the trial court should have selected M&M or allowed both firms to work together. The appeals court rejected this challenge, saying the trial court had the authority to choose counsel when the representatives could not agree.It found no reason to overturn the selection of KR&T. The firm had lawyers licensed in Kentucky, where the wrongful-death case was being pursued. The difference between the proposed fees was also not enough to show that the trial court had made an improper choice.Daniels will thus remain the sole personal representative of Fields' estate, with KR&T handling the wrongful-death claim.You use AI every day.
